2607.02374.title: DRIFTLENS: Measuring Memory-Induced Reasoning Drift in Personalized Language Models
2607.02374.paper_summary: Personalization changes what a model says to a user; we show that it can also change the reasoning trajectory used to justify the response. Modern LLMs personalize interactions by storing user attributes, preferences, and prior context, then injecting this information into future prompts. We study whether such memory reshapes reasoning on open-ended questions where no single ground-truth answer exists. To quantify this effect, we introduce DRIFTLENS, a ground-truth-free framework that maps each expressed reasoning step to a value category and measures divergence between a question's no-memory trajectory and its trajectory under injected user-attribute memory. We first validate that DRIFTLENS distinguishes content-free pragmatic noise from substantive reasoning changes. Across four LLMs and 10 user-attribute categories, including age, occupation, and disability, user-attribute memory induces medium-to-large reasoning drift above each model's pragmatic-noise floor, even when final answers remain fluent, on-topic, and plausible. We then evaluate GRPO- and DPO-based post-training methods for reducing drift. Both reduce drift, but neither uniformly dominates; effects on downstream capability, helpfulness, and instruction following are model-and reward-dependent. These results suggest that memory-induced reasoning drift is a measurable and only partly mitigated failure mode of personalized language models.
2607.02374.paper_summary_zh: 個性化改變了模型對用戶的表達；我們顯示它也可以改變用來證明回應的推理軌跡。現代大型語言模型通過儲存用戶屬性、偏好和先前的上下文來個性化互動，然後將這些信息注入未來的提示中。我們研究這種記憶是否改變了對於沒有單一真實答案的開放式問題的推理。為了量化這一效果，我們引入了DRIFTLENS，一個無需真實答案的框架，將每個表達的推理步驟映射到一個價值類別，並測量問題的無記憶軌跡與其在注入用戶屬性記憶下的軌跡之間的差異。我們首先驗證DRIFTLENS能夠區分無內容的務實噪音與實質性推理變化。在四個大型語言模型和10個用戶屬性類別中，包括年齡、職業和殘疾，用戶屬性記憶在每個模型的務實噪音基準之上引起中到大程度的推理漂移，即使最終答案仍然流暢、相關且合理。我們接著評估基於GRPO和DPO的後訓練方法以減少漂移。兩者都減少了漂移，但都沒有統一主導；對下游能力、有用性和遵循指令的影響依賴於模型和獎勵。這些結果表明，記憶引起的推理漂移是一種可測量且僅部分緩解的個性化語言模型的失效模式。
